report.summary:
WP-37 round 3. I fixed both major findings and the six minor findings I could see at their root cause, each with tests. The relayed minor list was cut off partway through the clip finding (see deviations).

MAJOR 1: stage G cost was not linear on input with errors. Each class member below has its own test, and each test fails on the code before this change.
- Keyed-entry ancestors and set-element ancestors (normalize.go): each step now records how many diagnostics existed when it was pushed. report() builds the path in O(depth) with placeholders for list elements (stack.prefix). pop() names a list element once, after it is fully normalized, by its key member or its RFC 8785 text, and fills that name into every diagnostic recorded below it. Paths therefore name elements in their hub form. TestNormalizeElementNames covers this; the old code named a set element half-normalized.
- own(): a converter's diagnostics are now resolved by one shared finder (lookup.go) instead of a walk from the root per diagnostic. The finder indexes each large object, each keyed list (per key member) and each set once: string, number (text or double), bool, null and raw RFC 8785 items, all first-match like tree.Node.At. TestFinderMatchesAt and FuzzFinder compare it against tree.Node.At. TestOwnScaleLinear covers keyed entries, object members, string sets, number sets and object sets.
- The locator's stack builds one path per failed decode (TestLocatorScaleLinear; see deviations).
- Before and after:
  - 96,000 null members after the cap: 9.6e8 work units before, 7.5e5 after.
  - 500,000 members (9 MB): 94 ms and 3.7e6 units, against the reported 10-20 s and 5e9 units.
  - The verifier's 160,000-member probe: 53 ms, was 3.48 s.
- Docs updated: package doc, Normalize, own, path/prefix/pop.

MAJOR 2: the keeper rendered every diagnostic's path.
- keep.go no longer renders paths. compareEntries compares paths only when environment, file, line, column and code all tie, and then with comparePaths. comparePaths skips the leading elements both paths share and renders the rest one element at a time up to the first differing byte. TestComparePaths checks that it orders exactly as strings.Compare of Path.String.
- Run's memory doc now says what is actually held at a time.
- Measured: Run on a 100,000-byte jwt issuer key or api-key member name with 10,001 diagnostics allocated 1,065 MB extra before; now 0.6 MB extra, peak heap about 23 MB (was 1,034 MB).
- diag.List.Sort still renders paths eagerly and takes 6.4 s on that result. It is a WP-01 contract, so it is filed as a contract request.

MINORS:
- (a) RZ-CFG-025 now has a caller. Stage.resource calls Registry.DeprecationsCounted on the authored tree before materialize. Its warnings use the diagnostic budget, and its walk counts toward the worker's yield timer. Deprecations also skips tree.StyleDefaulted nodes.
- (b) The locator now sees what the config decode sees (declaredOnly). This covers three class members: the struct case, the Go map case, and a type with its own UnmarshalJSON, which gets the filtered text.
- (c) The chunker decodes a large member straight into its field only when no other member the decode sees folds to the same name (foldName is exactly strings.EqualFold). Otherwise it uses a one-member batch, which keeps encoding/json's merge. Covered shapes: a top-level member, a member through a struct field of the envelope, a Unicode long-s fold, and the reverse member order. Added a FuzzChunkedDecode seed and TestChunkedDecodeFoldSplits (in a config only declared members count).
- (d) TestRegistryDefaults now also compares against a literal 02 req 13 table of all 23 types.
- (e) Deprecations no longer builds schema path strings. Each position narrows a binary-search range over the sorted table keys by its own segment, and no walk goes below a position that no deprecated path starts. No path text is built. The existing schema-path oracle test still passes.
- (f) clip in both packages reads at most 65 code points and allocates only its result.

Class members I reviewed and left unchanged:
- Messages that quote values: number, duration, byte size, apiVersion and the locator all go through the fixed clip.
- byteSizeMessage: it allocates a quoted copy of the value once per value node, which is linear.
- The keyed()/set() duplicate naming: once per duplicate entry, which is linear.
report.checks:
Scoped to ./internal/config/defaults/... and ./internal/config/convert/...:
- go build and go vet: clean. gofmt -l: empty.
- go test -race -count=1 -cover -shuffle=on: pass. Coverage is 97.5% for defaults and 98.9% for convert.
- CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1: pass. go test -short: pass.
- bin/golangci-lint run: 0 issues. bin/golangci-lint fmt --diff: empty.
- go run ./internal/tool/repocheck: exit 0.
- Fuzz, 60 s each, all pass: FuzzFinder (1.31M execs), FuzzChunkedDecode (1.48M), FuzzStageIdempotent (1.32M), FuzzIntegerText (1.30M), FuzzConversionRoundTrip (2.99M).

Fail-before proofs (go test -overlay with the pre-change sources backed up in scratchpad/wp37r3/orig):
- TestScaleLinearErrors, keyed nulls and keyed big integers: ratio 63.5 below the cap; 1.2e8 and 9.6e8 units above it, against a bound of 8 units per byte.
- TestScaleLinearErrors, set twin: 64x the units and bytes; the 96,000-member run was OOM-killed at 6.7 GB.
- TestOwnScaleLinear: all 5 shapes fail, ratios 63.7 to 70.
- TestRunLongKeyMemory: +1,065 MB for both inputs.
- TestKeeperTiedLongPaths: fails on allocation.
- TestNormalizeElementNames: the old code named the element half-normalized.
- TestLocatorDeclaredOnly (proof copy): blamed REQUESTS.
- Chunker fold cases: 3 of 3 fail on the old chunker.
- TestDeprecationsLongName: 2.13 GB. TestDeprecationsAuthoredOnly: fails.
- TestClipBounded: 67 MB allocated, in both packages.
- TestStageDeprecations: the old code gave no warnings.
- TestRegistryDefaults kills a mutation of the ratelimit failureMode in the registry; the old test let it pass.

Mutation run (scratchpad/wp37r3/mutate.py, results in mutations.txt): all 25 mutations killed. They cover each locator skip and filter, the chunker fold check and fold counting, foldName, pop/push/report naming, each finder index (keyed, numbers, raw, scalar raw), own reusing the finder, the keeper path comparison, sameElem and the '.' rule, the stage Deprecations call, its count and its order, the defaulted skip, the count hook, the segment dot, and both clip functions.

TestLocatorScaleLinear passes on both old and new code; that is the evidence for the locator deviation.

Integration measurement: 500,000 members (9 MB) take 94 ms and 3.7e6 units in stage G; the 15 MB out-of-range-integer variant takes 278 ms.
contractRequests: internal/config/diag (WP-01 contract), three changes. (a) List.Sort (diag.go:294-305) should compare Path only when Environment, File, Line, Column and Code tie: cmp.Or evaluates every argument, so today every comparison renders both paths' Path.String(). Measured on the 10,001 diagnostics that stage G now returns in 23 MB for a 100,000-byte jwt issuer key, List.Sort takes 6.4 s and allocates over 1 GB; with a 100,000-byte api-key member name it takes 3.7 s. Paths should also be compared without being rendered whole. Add `func (p Path) Compare(q Path) int` with the order of strings.Compare(p.String(), q.String()): skip the leading elements that are equal in kind and value, then render the rest one element at a time. internal/config/defaults/keep.go comparePaths, sameElem and appendElemText are a tested implementation (TestComparePaths) that diag can adopt; stage G would then call diag's. (b) Bound the text of each path element in Path.String, Diagnostic.AppendText and Path.MarshalJSON/WriteJSON. For example, clip member names, keys and set items to 64 code points (as stage G clips quoted values) with a marker, or state a byte budget per diagnostic. Today 10,001 diagnostics below one 100 KB key print about 1 GB of path text. (c) Spec 01 req 50: state the diagnostics cap in bytes as well as in count (for example, at most 10,000 diagnostics and N MiB of diagnostic text per run).

deviations: The relayed minor-findings list was cut off partway through the clip finding (at '...or a for-range loop over the string with a counter'). I fixed the clip finding as far as it was written (both packages). I could not see any minor findings after it, so none are addressed.

Locator's stack (named as a class member of major 1): the locator was not quadratic. It builds one path per failed decode, and a decode reports at most one failure per resource, so each element on the path is named once. Evidence: TestLocatorScaleLinear (a failure in the last of 1,000 or 8,000 keyed entries) shows about 8x the work units on both the old and the new code. I documented this on locator and stack.path rather than adding a cache that would never be hit twice.

I did not add ctx reads inside a resource (the finding said 'consider'). Spec 01 req 53 says 'ctx is checked between units', and Run keeps that. With the fix, one resource costs linear work: 94 ms for 500,000 failing members (9 MB), so a 64 MiB resource is on the order of 1 s.

TestRunLongKeyMemory bounds the extra allocation a 100,000-byte key adds (at most 16 copies of the key; it was 10,001) rather than total allocation as a small multiple of the source size. The 10,001 capped diagnostics cost about 26 MB on their own (about 2.6 KB each, independent of the key) for an 18-byte-per-diagnostic source, so a total bound would not isolate the defect.

The set-element twin of the error scale tests uses a test-only rendered schema (setSchemaJSON in scale_test.go). Every ruralz/v1alpha1 set holds strings or closed two-string objects, so no v1alpha1 input can put a diagnostic inside a set element. The finding allowed this.
